solutions.latex:
$f(x)=3x^2+5x$

$$f(x+h)=3(x+h)^2+5(x+h)=3x^2+6hx+3h^2+5x+5h$$

$$f(x+h)-f(x)=3x^2+6hx+3h^2+5x+5h-(3x^2+5x)=6xh+3h^2+5h$$

$$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{6xh+3h^2+5h}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\,(6x+3h+5)$$

Apply the limit by letting $h=0$:

$$\therefore \dfrac{dy}{dx}=6x+5$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: Provides correct solution; 1: Finds correct expression for $f(x+h)-f(x)$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$$y=\dfrac{\ln(x-1)}{x-1}$$

Using quotient rule:

$$y'=\dfrac{\frac{1}{x-1}\times(x-1)-\ln(x-1)}{(x-1)^2}=\dfrac{1-\ln(x-1)}{(x-1)^2}$$

At the point where $x=2$, gradient of tangent is given by

$$\dfrac{1-\ln(2-1)}{(2-1)^2}=1$$

Hence, the gradient of the normal is $-1$.

Using the point-gradient formula to find the equation of the normal:

$$y-0=-1(x-2)$$

$$\therefore y=2-x$$

12 000 cm represents total perimeter robot can draw, so divide by 4 so series is in terms of side length, not perimeter.

Total sum of side lengths is given by $12\,000\div4=3000$

Solve for $n$ the sum formula $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2a+(n-1)d\big)$ where $S_n=3000$, $a=5$, $d=3$

$$3000=\dfrac{n}{2}\big(2\times5+(n-1)3\big)$$

$$6000=n(10+3n-3)$$

$$6000=3n^2+7n$$

$$3n^2+7n-6000=0$$

Using quadratic formula, $n=-45.9$ or $n=43.6$ but $n>0$ so negative answer in invalid

43.6 means robot draws 43 complete squares plus part of the 44th square.

$\therefore$ Robot can draw 43 complete squares with one pen

Based on the transformed data and using REG mode on calculator, equation of the least-squares regression is

$$\ln(y)=1.124x+2.85$$

The value of $\ln(y)$ in the 7th year is given by

$$\ln(y)=1.124\times7+2.85=10.718$$

Hence, the value of $y$ is given by

Signed area between curves $P$ and $Q$ represents the relative displacement between both cars.

Cars are at exactly the same displacement from starting point when displacement between cars is zero.

Solve for $a$:

$$\int_0^a 3t^2-6t+4-(6t+4)\,dt=0$$

$$\int_0^a 3t^2-12t\,dt=0$$

$$\Big[t^3-6t^2\Big]_0^a=0$$

$$a^3-6a^2=0$$

$$a^2(a-6)=0,\quad a>0$$

Hence cars are at the same distance away from the start at $t=6$.

The integrand $3t^2-12t$ represents velocity of $P$ relative to $Q$.

For $t>4$, $v_P>v_Q$ Hence car $P$ will pass car $Q$ after 6 seconds from start of race.

solutions.latex:
$$f'(x)=-1+x-x^2+x^3-\cdots$$

This is s geometric series with first term $-1$ and common ratio $-x$

Since $0<x<1$, the geometric series will have a limiting sum.

Hence,

$$f'(x)=S_\infty=\dfrac{-1}{1+x}$$

$$f(x)=-\int\dfrac{1}{1+x}\,dx=-\ln(1+x)+C$$

$$f(a)-f(b)=-\ln(1+a)-\big(-\ln(1+b)\big)$$

$$=\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{1+a}\right)-\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{1+b}\right)$$

$$=\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{1+a}\div\dfrac{1}{1+b}\right)$$

$$=\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{1+a}\times\dfrac{1+b}{1}\right)$$

$$=\ln\left(\dfrac{1+b}{1+a}\right)$$

solutions.latex:
Solve simultaneously the equations $y=x+d$ and $(x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=9$

By substitution:

$$(x-1)^2+(x+d-3)^2=9$$

$$(x-1)^2+\big(x+(d-3)\big)^2=9$$

$$x^2-2x+1+x^2+2x(d-3)+(d+3)^2=9$$

$$x^2-2x+1+x^2+2dx-6x+d^2-6d+9=9$$

$$2x^2+2dx-8x+d^2-6d+1=0$$

$$2x^2+(2d-8)x+(d^2-6d+1)=0$$

This is a non-monic quadratic equation with 2 distinct real solutions if discriminant $D>0$.

$$D=(2d-8)^2-4(2)(d^2-6d+1)=4d^2-32d+64-8d^2+48d-8=-4d^2+16d+56$$

Use quadratic formula to find values of $d$ when $D=0$:

$$d=\dfrac{-16\pm\sqrt{(16)^2+4(4)(56)}}{2(-4)}=\dfrac{-16\pm\sqrt{1152}}{-8}=\dfrac{-16\pm24\sqrt{2}}{-8}=2\pm3\sqrt{2}$$

Graph of $D$ is a concave down parabola with roots $2\pm3\sqrt{2}$ hence $D>0$ in the interval

$$2-3\sqrt{2}<d<2+3\sqrt{2}$$

$\therefore$ $\ell$ intersects $C$ at exactly two points if $2-3\sqrt{2}<d<2+3\sqrt{2}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Provides correct solution; 2: Recognises that discriminant $>0$ for 2 distinct real solutions and attempts to use quadratic formula to find values of $d$, or equivalent merit; 1: Finds an equation involving $x$ and $d$ by solving equation of $\ell$ and $C$ simultaneously, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Solving the equation from part (a) to find $x$ coordinates of $A$ and $B$:

$$2x^2+(2d-8)x+d^2-6d+1=0$$

$$x_1=\dfrac{8-2d-\sqrt{D}}{4}=2-\dfrac{d}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{4}$$

$$x_2=\dfrac{8-2d+\sqrt{D}}{4}=2-\dfrac{d}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{4}$$

Using the equation $y=x+d$ to find corresponding $y$-coordinates:

$$y_1=2+\dfrac{d}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{4},\quad y_2=2+\dfrac{d}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{4}$$

Using the distance formula:

$$\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2}\right)^2}=2\sqrt{3}$$

$$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{D}}{2}\right)^2=12$$

$$D=24$$

Solving $-4d^2+16d+56=24$ by first dividing all terms by $(-4)$:

$$d^2-4d-8=0$$

$$d=2\pm2\sqrt{3}$$

$\therefore$ Possible values of $d$ are $2-2\sqrt{3}$ or $2+2\sqrt{3}$.
